# How to approach a math mixed contest

Math tasks seldom announce their technique. The task is to turn the story into
a precise object before reaching for a formula.

# Complete local contest set

| Problem | Title |
|---|---|
| A | Blocked Path |
| B | Coprime Pairs |
| C | At Least One |
| D | Complete Alphabet |
| E | Modular Appointment |
| F | Festival Synchronization |
| G | Capped Allocation |
| H | GCD-One Subsets |
| I | Exactly K Colors |
| J | Target LCM Subsets |
| K | Weighted Coupon Collection |
| L | Random Divisor Descent |

Problems F through L form the harder half of the contest. They deliberately
combine tools instead of isolating one chapter at a time:

| Problem | Combination to recognize |
|---|---|
| F | recognize and apply generalized CRT from Section 30 |
| G | stars and bars plus inclusion-exclusion over violated caps |
| H | divisor sieve plus subtraction of larger exact gcd classes |
| I | choose the used colors, then count surjections |
| J | target factorization plus bitmask union of required exponents |
| K | tail-sum expectation plus inclusion-exclusion over missing coupons |
| L | expectation recurrence evaluated by a divisor sieve |

For these problems, first write the slow or unrestricted mathematical model.
The efficient solution usually appears only after identifying repeated divisor
work, symmetric bad events, or a small set of prime-factor features.

# A diagnosis routine, not an answer key

For each local problem, write the following on paper:

```text
What set of objects am I counting, comparing, or assigning probability to?
What makes an object valid?
Can the desired set be partitioned into disjoint cases?
Would it be easier to count its complement or subtract bad objects?
Which assumption makes multiplication or division legal?
```

Do not infer a method merely from words such as "grid", "gcd", or "at least
one". The same words can support different models. The editorial contains the
local reductions after you have attempted them.

# Build formulas from bijections

Every multiplication should have a reason. A product is justified when every
object is represented by one independent choice from each factor, with neither
omissions nor duplicates. A subtraction is justified when the bad objects form
a set whose size you can count exactly. Inclusion-exclusion is appropriate
only after you identify the overlapping properties being counted.

For probability, distinguish disjoint events from independent events. Disjoint
probabilities add. Independent probabilities multiply. Neither property should
be assumed because it seems intuitive.

# Tiny-model validation

Before coding a closed form, enumerate a tiny instance by hand or with a
brute-force checker. Compare three things:

```text
the objects in the original statement
the objects your formula counts
the boundary cases excluded by the formula
```

This is especially important for empty choices, a value with no factors,
impossible states, and modular division.

# Complexity and arithmetic

Let the largest constraint determine the shape of the solution. If values have
a bounded universe, preprocessing may be useful; if a formula contains many
queries, precomputation may be necessary. State the cost of every loop and the
largest possible intermediate value, not only the final answer.

When working modulo a prime, division means multiplying by an inverse, and
only denominators with an inverse are legal. Use `long long` for C++ modular
products before reducing. In Python, still reduce deliberately so values and
intent remain clear.

# Common mistakes

```text
Using a product without proving independent choices.
Subtracting overlapping bad sets without correcting double counts.
Treating non-disjoint events as independent.
Forgetting empty or degenerate cases.
Using modular division when the inverse does not exist.
```

# Exercises

Attempt A through L without naming a prior technique. For each one, write the
mathematical object, one candidate counting identity, and a tiny example that
would falsify that identity. Open the editorial only after the identity and
its assumptions are explicit.

Run the local checker after the paper trace:

```bash
CP_TARGET=solution python3 sections/35_math_mixed_contest/check.py
```
